title: AIV audit report (rubric v1.1+)
description: Emit this and your results are comparable with anyone else's. v2 replaces v1 because rubric v1.1 changed the output shape: a single `score` became `readiness` reported alongside an unscored citation block, checks carry the tier they reached rather than a pass/fail verdict, and gate checks can cap the total. v1 stays published — reports written against rubric v1.0 remain valid under it.

rubric_version.description: The rubric this was scored against. A score without it is not comparable to anything.

tool.description: Which implementation produced this report, e.g. "geo-score-cli/1.1.0". Optional, but it makes two reports of the same site comparable — a heuristic tool and a human auditor will legitimately differ on the judgement-bound checks.

elapsed_s.description: Seconds the scoring run took, from the first request to the last answer, as measured on the machine that ran it. It depends on that machine's network as much as on the site, so it describes the run, not the site, and a comparison of two reports ignores it. Optional; added in 1.5.0.

audience_language.description: BCP 47 primary tag of the most common language among the sampled pages (en, ja, de, …), ties going to the page sampled first; Chinese is written zh-CN, as it was when the field was either that or en, and und means no page's language could be told. Each page is read in its own language: answer passages in characters (50–200) for Chinese, Japanese and Korean pages and in words (25–120) for all others, and the heading, source-phrase and byline lexicons (English and Chinese) read only pages in their languages.

sampled_urls.description: The pages scored. Exactly 8 unless the site has fewer pages; if fewer, say so in notes. The CLI leaves out a sampled page that answered with an error or a bot-challenge page, and its notes then say how many of how many sampled pages were scored and why (since 1.5.0).

landed.description: Present when the site redirected to a different domain: the URL that was actually scored. Optional; added in 1.3.0.

sample_source.description: Where the sample came from: "sitemap", homepage and section links when no sitemap was reachable, or "pinned" when the pages were given with --urls or --urls-from. Two runs that sampled different pages usually differ here.

id.description: A check id from rubric v1.1. Ids are permanent.

state.description: No `failed` state: under tiered scoring a check that meets nothing is `scored` at tier 1 with 0 points, which keeps it in the denominator. `unobservable` and `not_applicable` leave the denominator.

points.description: The tier actually reached. Required when state is `scored`.

tier_reason.description: Why this tier and not the next one up. This is the line a reader acts on.

doc_url.description: Where this check is defined in the rubric, pinned to the tool's release tag. Optional; added in 1.3.0.

evidence.description: Reproducible observation: status codes, byte counts, hashes, N of 8 pages, the actual sentence.

allOf.description: A scored check must show the tier it reached and the evidence for it. Bonus checks (ids starting b.) are not tiered, so they need no tier_reason.

readiness.description: Sum of scored points including bonus. Bonus caps at +6 and stays out of the denominator.

observable_max.description: Sum of max for checks still in the denominator. Never 100 unless nothing was excluded.

normalised.description: min(100, round(100 × readiness / observable_max)), capped at 40 when a gate check scored zero (gate_capped); bonus points count in readiness, so the 100 ceiling matters.

band.description: Band name in either English or Chinese, exactly as the rubric spells it.

gate_capped.description: True when g.robots, g.reachable or g.ssr scored zero, which caps normalised at 40 and leads the report; a gate at a middle tier is a deduction, not a cap.

citation.description: Whether engines actually cite the site. An outcome, never summed into readiness. Omit the object entirely rather than reporting a zero you did not measure.

channel.description: api = provider APIs with web search (geo-score --ask / watch); app = sampled by hand in the consumer apps. Never pool the two.

excluded.description: Every check that left the denominator, with why. Without this the max is unexplainable.

notes.description: The auditor's own caveats. An audit that hides its blind spots is worth less than a lower score.

access.description: Observations about how crawlers reach the site's pages and what the pages tell them about their language versions, reported outside the score: nothing here enters readiness, observable_max or normalised, and the rubric does not define them. URLs and robots.txt rules are in the form RFC 9309 section 2.2.2 compares them in (percent-encoding normalised). Optional.

robots_paths.description: robots.txt page by page. g.robots reads only a Disallow that closes the whole site; this holds the homepage, every sampled page and the first 200 URLs on the audited host and path of the sitemap p1.sitemap read (the first child of a sitemap index) against the rules each retrieval crawler of reference/ai-crawlers.md obeys (the group RFC 9309 section 2.2.1 picks for it), read two ways: RFC 9309 section 2.2.2 (the longest matching pattern decides, an allow wins a tie, * and a final $ are wildcards) and the first-match reading of Python's urllib.robotparser and many older checkers (rules in file order, the first plain prefix decides). When the homepage redirects to another host (apex to www, a rename), the sitemap's URLs on that host are checked too if robots.txt was answered from there. Only the first 500 KiB of robots.txt are read, the least RFC 9309 section 2.5 asks a crawler to parse, and the readings stop after 1,000,000 rule comparisons (see not_checked). No request is made for it.

robots_txt.description: read: robots.txt answered 2xx. absent: it answered 4xx, so nothing is disallowed (RFC 9309 2.3.1.3). unreadable: no answer, or 429 or 5xx on every try; blocked and read_differently are then null (not observed).

checked.description: URLs checked: the homepage, the sampled pages and the sitemap URLs, each once.

not_checked.description: URLs left unchecked because robots.txt carries so many rules that the readings reached their limit of 1,000,000 rule comparisons first (a file of thousands of wildcard rules); 0 otherwise. The counts and lists cover the checked URLs only.

crawlers.description: Retrieval crawlers each URL was checked for.

blocked.description: Checked URLs that the RFC 9309 reading closes to at least one retrieval crawler.

one_rule.description: True when every blocked page is closed by one and the same rule to the same crawlers, as a Disallow: / in one group does; the views then say it in one line. False when nothing is blocked or robots.txt was not read.

pages.description: The first 50 of them, in the order checked.

read_differently.description: Checked URLs where the two readings disagree, allowed against blocked, for at least one retrieval crawler.

differences.description: The first 50 of them, each reading with the rule that decided it.

rule.description: The rule that decided, as "Allow: /path" or "Disallow: /path", or null when no rule matches (the page is allowed).
The rule that decided, as "Allow: /path" or "Disallow: /path", or null when no rule matches (the page is allowed).

server_links.description: Links in the server HTML: the <a href> links a crawler that runs no JavaScript can follow, read from the pages the run fetched (the homepage, the sampled pages and the section indexes its sampling read), outside comments, scripts, styles and templates. Each page's links resolve against the URL it was answered from. A link is to a page on this site when it resolves to the audited host and path, or to the host the homepage redirected to (apex to www, a rename); the host's letter case, Unicode or punycode form and the scheme do not matter, and fragments, queries and a trailing slash are dropped. javascript:, mailto: and tel: links are not links to a page. Only the fetched pages are searched, so a URL none of them links to is not shown to be orphaned. No request is made for it.

pages_searched.description: Fetched pages whose server HTML was searched for links, each once.

home_links.description: Pages on this site the homepage's server HTML links to, the homepage itself left out; null when the homepage was not fetched (a pinned sample without it, or an error).

few_home_links.description: home_links is below 3: navigation that appears only after JavaScript runs cannot be followed by crawlers that do not run it.

other_sampled.description: Sampled pages other than the homepage.

home_links_to_sampled.description: How many of them the homepage's server HTML links to; null when the homepage was not fetched.

sitemap_urls.description: Sitemap URLs checked: the first 200 on this site that the sitemap p1.sitemap read lists (the first child of a sitemap index), the homepage aside, since a crawl starts there.

sitemap_urls_linked.description: Of them, those the server HTML of at least one searched page links to, a page's link to itself left out.

unlinked_sitemap_urls.description: The first 50 of the others, in sitemap order.

hreflang.description: hreflang annotations on the pages the run fetched (the homepage, the sampled pages and the section indexes its sampling read), reported as found: each <link> whose rel names alternate and that has an hreflang and an href, outside comments, scripts, styles and templates, anywhere in the server HTML (a link whose type names something other than HTML, as a feed's does, is left out), and each link in the page's HTTP Link header (RFC 8288) with rel alternate and an hreflang parameter, every Link line read. Annotations from a sitemap are not read. Each href resolves against the URL its page was answered from; two URLs name one page when their host, path (without a trailing slash, percent-encoding normalised) and query match, whatever the scheme and fragment. Codes are held to the subset of BCP 47 that Google's hreflang documentation supports: an ISO 639-1 language, optionally an ISO 15924 script, optionally an officially assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region, or x-default, in any letter case. Return links are checked only between the fetched pages. Codes and hrefs as written are shown with each character outside printable ASCII, and each of ' <>"{}|\^`', percent-encoded. Only the first 1,000 annotations of a page are read (see not_read). No request is made for it.

pages_searched.description: Fetched pages read for annotations, each once.

pages_with_hreflang.description: Of them, those that carry at least one annotation.

annotations.description: Annotations read on them, in the HTML and in Link headers.

pages_with_link_header.description: Pages that carry annotations in their HTTP Link header.

pages.description: The first 50 pages that carry annotations, with how many.

url.description: The annotated page, as it was answered (scheme and host as given, path and query in the form RFC 9309 section 2.2.2 compares them in).

no_self_reference.description: Pages with annotations none of which names the page itself (its requested or its answered URL).

invalid_codes.description: Codes outside the subset, counted once per page and code (letter case aside).

url.description: The annotated page, as it was answered (scheme and host as given, path and query in the form RFC 9309 section 2.2.2 compares them in).

hreflang.description: The code as written, cut at 64 characters.

problem.description: form: not language[-Script][-REGION] (an underscore, a word, a fourth part). language: two or three letters that are no ISO 639-1 code (a two-letter subtag of the IANA Language Subtag Registry). region: no officially assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (UK, EU, UN, or a three-digit area such as 419).

duplicate_codes.description: Codes that name more than one page on the same page (letter case aside), counted once per page and code.

url.description: The annotated page, as it was answered (scheme and host as given, path and query in the form RFC 9309 section 2.2.2 compares them in).

urls.description: How many pages the code names there.

not_absolute.description: Annotations whose href, as written, is not an absolute http or https URL (a relative path, no scheme, or another scheme), counted once per page and href.

not_absolute_hrefs.description: The first 50 of them, as written.

url.description: The annotated page, as it was answered (scheme and host as given, path and query in the form RFC 9309 section 2.2.2 compares them in).

other_host.description: Annotations naming a URL on a host that is not this site's (the audited host, or the one its homepage redirected to), counted once per page and URL. hreflang allows it; it is noted only.

url.description: The annotated page, as it was answered (scheme and host as given, path and query in the form RFC 9309 section 2.2.2 compares them in).

pairs_checked.description: Pairs of fetched pages in which at least one names the other.

one_way.description: Of them, pairs in which only one names the other.

one_way_pairs.description: The first 50 of them: from names to, and to does not name from back.

targets_not_fetched.description: Other pages the annotations name that the run did not fetch: their return links are not checked.

not_read.description: Annotations past the first 1,000 of a page, counted and not read; the other counts and lists cover the ones read. 0 on any real page.
